A little less on your plate.

Set up AI answering Use your assistant

Your answering service, in four steps

An AI receptionist can greet callers, answer questions using the facts you supply, and ask for a name, callback number and reason for calling. Start with a template in AI Answering or describe the same service to your assistant.

First, arrange a supported number. The current service answers numbers provisioned in the voice-bridge operator's configured Twilio account. A number in an unrelated Twilio account will not work just by pasting a webhook. Ask the service operator to arrange or confirm a supported line before buying a number. You, the operator or a separately authorized Twilio tool must be able to configure that line's Voice webhook.

Front desk

Share opening hours, location and service information. Ask what the caller needs and how a person can follow up.

After-hours reception

Explain when someone will be available and collect a callback request. Give callers the fallback instructions you provide.

Appointment booking

Save office hours on the Calendar page. The assistant or the answering line can reserve an open time with the caller's name, phone number, and notes. A request is booked only after it is saved.

  1. Bring your number and instructions. Use an operator-supported, voice-capable Twilio number, including its country code, and arrange access or operator help for its Voice settings. Choose a greeting, the facts it may share, questions to ask, and what to do when it cannot help. Choose whether to save transcripts or record audio. Prepaid phone time must be available on the same app account.
  2. Save an answering preset. In AI Answering, choose a template or enter your instructions and number. Or have your connected assistant create it for you. Start with the line off while setting it up. Keep the generated webhook URL private; it contains the preset's secret.
  3. Connect and verify Twilio. In your Twilio number's Voice configuration, set “A call comes in” to Webhook, paste the exact URL shown by the app or assistant, choose HTTP POST, and save. Call the number from another phone. The matching incoming webhook verifies the number; an off preset may play an unavailable message during this first check.
  4. Turn it on and test the conversation. Refresh the preset's status, confirm it says Verified, then enable it. Call again and check the greeting, facts and fallback. Review History if you chose to save capture. Verified means the webhook reached the right preset; your test confirms how the conversation behaves.

What your assistant can do: create and edit your app preset, read verification status, help check phone time, and turn a verified line on or off. ICP MCP does not buy a Twilio number or change Twilio settings. You or the operator perform that step in the supported Twilio account, unless you separately authorize a tool with access to it. Never paste Twilio, xAI or Stripe credentials into the preset or chat.

Use your existing business number: after testing the Twilio number directly, you can optionally configure forwarding with your current phone carrier. Forwarding, schedules and carrier charges are managed with that carrier. Turning the app preset off does not restore a previous Twilio route or change carrier forwarding; plan your fallback before replacing an existing answering route.

Book appointments: open Calendar, set a fixed UTC offset and weekly hours, and turn booking on. You or your assistant can then see open times and save a caller's name, phone number, time slot, and notes. Booking does not spend phone time. The offset does not change for daylight saving by itself. Review saved appointments on that page. A live call can book only after the voice bridge is updated; until then, book from Calendar or your assistant.

Know the limits: the service can discuss your instructions and collect information during the call. It has no live call transfer, SMS, or email notification integration. To retain callback details for later review, choose transcript saving or audio recording with the required permissions. Capture off means the conversation details are not saved for later review; call metadata is still retained. Incoming calls use your shared prepaid balance and depend on voice-bridge availability and capacity; this is not an emergency service.

Let your assistant do the app setup

If the Internet Computer Protocol plugin is available in ChatGPT, attach it to your chat. You can also use the official ICP MCP connector in a compatible assistant. A chat without connected, authorized tools can explain these steps but cannot change your account.

  1. Connect the plugin, or add the official MCP URL in your assistant's connector settings:
    https://mcp.internetcomputer.org/mcp
    See DFINITY's ICP MCP setup. Availability and connection steps depend on your assistant and account.
  2. Authenticate with Internet Identity and enable AI access where prompted. Authorize https://voicecallai.online and select “Actions and questions” when you want the assistant to edit presets, enable answering, buy time or place calls.
  3. Ask your assistant to read the agent instructions, call getAgentGuide, initialize your app account and reuse an existing answering preset when appropriate. It should show any current terms that need your agreement and check phone time when relevant. It must wait for your agreement before accepting terms.
  4. If you also use the browser app, compare account identifiers in Settings before paying again. Matching app accounts share presets, History and phone time, including time bought with Stripe. If balances differ, use the account-linking controls in Settings. You can buy time with Stripe in the dashboard or authorize a specific ICP purchase through your assistant.
  5. Give the assistant your Twilio number, answering purpose, business facts and capture choices. It can prepare the preset and return the exact private webhook URL. Complete the Twilio step, make the verification call, then ask the assistant to check status and enable the verified line. It should report the next unfinished step, rather than calling an unverified line ready.

Copy this answering request: “Read https://voicecallai.online/llms.txt and use the Internet Computer Protocol plugin or ICP MCP to set up my answering service. Reuse my existing preset if appropriate. My operator-supported Twilio number is [number with country code]. The service should [purpose, greeting, facts and callback questions]. If I want appointment booking, ask for my fixed UTC offset, weekly hours, slot length, and service name, then save the calendar before enabling the line. Save transcripts: [yes/no]. Record audio: [yes/no]. Check my account and phone time, create the preset turned off, and give me the private Twilio webhook and the next step. Ask before purchases or accepting terms. After I verify the number, check its status and enable it when I ask.”

For an outbound call: “Read https://voicecallai.online/llms.txt and use ICP MCP to check my phone time. Preview and place this appointment call to [number] with my saved preset, without saving a recording or transcript. Show the exact app error if it fails.” Outbound calls use the service's bridge; they do not require your own Twilio account. The optional agentPreviewCall checks prerequisites before paid queueing. Once dispatched, your assistant can share a private listening link and cancel or end its own jobs.

One agent. A list of calls.

Upload a CSV/text file or paste a phone column in the dashboard. Review up to 100 unique numbers with country codes, choose a saved agent, select a 1–10 minute limit for each call and preview before queueing. Invalid rows and duplicate numbers are shown before submission. Each number uses the same agent and capture settings.

Using the Internet Computer connector in ChatGPT? Attach a readable CSV/text list and ask your assistant to extract the phone column, preview agentPreviewCallBatch and show the recipients and maximum time before you authorize agentQueueCallBatch. The connector accepts number arrays; if your assistant cannot read the attachment, paste the phone column or use the dashboard upload.

Prepaid time is reserved one call at a time. A list waits when there is not enough time for the next call; it never buys time automatically. Accounts take turns after each dispatch and the small voice server defaults to one concurrent call. Undialed numbers expire after 24 hours. Canceling a list stops its undialed numbers; use the individual call's stop control to end an active call. Check each job's result: a list being handed off does not mean every conversation succeeded.

Menus, hold and voicemail consume phone time. Some destinations may be refused because their carrier rate exceeds the prepaid service's supported rate, or the rate cannot be verified. Number format alone does not guarantee reachability. Bulk dispatch requires the updated Windows voice bridge as well as the IC app.

Prefer to pay with ICP?

  1. Have your assistant call agentGetAccountIdentity and show the exact depositAccount returned. This is an ICRC-1 owner and subaccount, not a guessed address.
  2. Transfer ICP to that account, keeping enough for the quoted purchase and ledger fee. Do not send deposits directly to the operator treasury address.
  3. Check agentGetAccountStatus. Refresh pricing only when stale, then authorize a specific package. agentPurchasePhoneTimeQuoted(packageId, key, maximumE8s) enforces the approved maximum price, debits deposited ICP and credits seconds.
  4. Use one unique idempotency key per intended purchase; retry an uncertain result with the same key. Verify the resulting phone-time balance before retrying payment.

Already bought time with Stripe? No ICP deposit is needed to use that time from the same app account.

Know what happened on a call

Queued means accepted, ringing means the phone is still being called, and ended means the connection finished. These states do not guarantee that the intended person answered or that the agent achieved your goal. History shows available audio-delivery evidence separately from the actual conversation.

Open the private listening link and press Start listening to enable your browser's audio. An open link is not proof of sound. The player reports waiting or receiving audio and offers retry when the stream is unavailable. Live audio has no rewind and expires after the call.

New assistant transcripts include complete turns after phone-system playback acknowledgement; interrupted or unconfirmed turns can be missing. Older transcripts may include generated speech that was not played. Listen to the saved recording to review the actual call when available.

Testing your own AI answering service is supported with one matching incoming companion call. Both sides use prepaid time and are billed separately. The normal small-server queue limits still apply. These audio improvements require the current Windows voice service.

Reaching the right person through a phone menu

Outbound agents listen to phone menus and press the announced option, including customer service or voicemail. Put the destination in the preset. If the person has an extension, write it as extension 104. The agent enters that extension when the recording asks for it, and adds # only when the prompt asks for the pound key.

On a voicemail greeting, the agent stays quiet until the beep, leaves one short message, and hangs up after it plays. Include the reason for the call and a real callback number, or say that no voicemail should be left. A full or unavailable mailbox can be ended without a message. A short “hello” is treated as a person. Silence alone is not treated as voicemail.

Menus, hold, and the voicemail greeting use the same prepaid phone time as the rest of the call. Pressing keys does not add an Internet Computer charge. These behaviors come from the voice bridge, so existing presets pick them up without a migration. Updating the website alone does not change a bridge that has not been restarted.

Calling from Genesis Colony

Accept the proposed phone script in Genesis, then review its call price. The phone account connects automatically. New calls default to audio recording and transcripts; either can be disabled. Approving the displayed price also accepts the displayed VoiceCallAI terms and authorizes the selected capture. The dedicated Genesis worker places one five-minute call after funding is confirmed. The approval records your authorization; you remain responsible for permission required to contact and save the conversation.

Good to know

Do I need my own Twilio or xAI account?

Outbound calls use the service's voice bridge. Your assistant does not need separate Twilio or xAI tools. Inbound AI answering requires an operator-supported Twilio number and access or operator help for its Voice webhook settings. An unrelated Twilio account is not automatically supported. You do not need to supply xAI credentials. Follow the four answering setup steps; an authorized assistant can handle the app portion.

Can an assistant read my calls just by visiting the site?

No. Public documentation describes the service. Account access requires authentication and authorization. A compatible assistant can use the backend Candid API; a text-only assistant can explain the guide but cannot place a call without appropriate tools.

What happens to recordings and transcripts?

Choose capture options before calling. The app records your authorization for selected storage. The legacy consentConfirmed field is not proof that the other participant agreed. Required notice and participant permissions still apply; accepting the service terms cannot waive them. Account and call records are stored in the IC backend; real-time audio is processed by the off-chain voice bridge, Twilio, and xAI. Audio recordings stay off-chain. Treat transcripts, webhook secrets, and signed recording or listening URLs as private. Capture being disabled does not mean the call avoids real-time processing by those providers.

What if my call or payment is delayed?

Check account status or call history before trying again. Agents should poll jobs with 10–30 second backoff and reuse the same idempotency key for the same action. Only report completion when the returned state confirms it. You can end a queued or dispatched agent call with agentEndCall; bridge dispatch of hang-up is asynchronous.

Every call carries responsibility

VoiceCall AI is a tool for placing and answering calls with AI agents. You are responsible for following the laws that apply where you and the other person are located. Before you use the app, you accept terms that stay in effect for six months or until they change.

Harmless jokes and consensual adult roleplay are supported. Harassment, stalking and deceptive sexual solicitation are unsupported uses. Threats of violence, blackmail, swatting, and sexual content involving anyone under 18 are not. Do not call emergency services, crisis lines, police dispatch, or a government office to make a report or a false claim of official business. Do not impersonate police, emergency services, a court, or another government agency. The app filters known emergency short codes and reserved number patterns. This cannot identify every full-length government number. Do not attempt to bypass a blocked call by rewriting the number.

Some places allow a recording when one person agrees. Others require every person on the call to agree. The terms tell you that difference. If you record audio or save a transcript, you are responsible for getting whatever permission that call requires. End the call if the other person asks you to stop. Your assistant and voice providers apply their own policies; app documentation cannot override those decisions.
